  "text": "The next morning, Mara returned to the workshop with the brass key and a list of questions. She had barely opened the door when a thin stream of sand slid from the ceiling and gathered on the floor in a perfect circle.

At its center sat a wooden box she had never seen before. The lid bore a carved map of the coastline, with a tiny silver pin marking a cove beyond the northern cliffs. Mara turned the key in the box’s lock. Inside lay a compass, a folded chart, and a note addressed to her.

“Some things are easier to hear when you are far from home,” her grandfather had written. “Take the path the needle chooses.”

The compass needle spun once, then settled toward the north. Mara packed bread, a water bottle, and her grandfather’s old raincoat. By noon, she had followed the cliff path to the cove, where waves boomed against black rocks.

A narrow opening in the cliff led to a chamber lit by greenish sunlight. On a ledge rested a glass bottle containing a rolled sheet of paper. Mara pulled out the message. It was not a map, but a list of names—families who had once lived along the shore before a storm scattered them inland.

At the bottom, her grandfather had added one final line: “A harbor is more than a place boats return to. It is a place people remember.”

Mara carried the list back to town. By evening, the dockmaster had found an old photograph showing several of the families gathered beside the clock tower. They began asking questions, and soon the harbor was full of stories that had waited years to be told."
